summary: Created a local CA "OS Comparison Root CA" on node1 (RSA-4096, self-signed, 10yr validity, proper CA basicConstraints/keyUsage) with key/cert stored in /etc/pki/os-comparison-ca/, installed its certificate into the AlmaLinux system trust store via /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and update-ca-trust extract, and verified via `trust list` and end-to-end leaf-certificate verification (openssl verify against the default system trust bundle) that the CA is genuinely trusted. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued a background `shutdown -r now` whose ack returned before disconnect, confirmed the node dropped, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (d6298ced... -> 1c1541e1...) proving an actual restart, and re-verified post-restart that the CA trust anchor persisted on disk and that a freshly issued leaf certificate still verifies against the system trust store.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and confirmed openssl/update-ca-trust availability
Generated 4096-bit CA private key and self-signed CA certificate CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, 3650-day validity, CA:TRUE basicConstraints, keyCertSign/cRLSign keyUsage
Copied CA cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/os-comparison-root-ca.pem and ran update-ca-trust extract
Confirmed CA listed as trusted anchor via `trust list`
Issued a test leaf certificate signed by the new CA and verified it against the default system trust store (openssl verify, no -CAfile) to prove functional trust
Cleaned up temp leaf cert files
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime -s baseline plus CA trust anchor state
Triggered `shutdown -r now` in background so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Confirmed connection drop (exec failure) then polled until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart CA trust anchor presence via `trust list` and file listing, and uptime -s showing new boot time
Re-ran end-to-end leaf certificate issuance/verification post-restart to prove CA trust persisted

evidence.requirement: CA 'OS Comparison Root CA' created on node1
evidence.summary: openssl generated CA key/cert; x509 -noout shows subject/issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA with proper CA basicConstraints/keyUsage extensions

evidence.requirement: CA certificate installed as trusted system CA
evidence.summary: Cert copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract run; trust list confirms 'OS Comparison Root CA' registered as an anchor/authority

evidence.requirement: Trust is functionally effective (not just file presence)
evidence.summary: A leaf cert issued by the new CA verifies successfully via `openssl verify` against the default system trust bundle

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + CA state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id d6298ced-a924-4ce7-bbed-0fb8179eda8e, pre-reboot uptime -s, and confirmed CA trust anchor and cert files present before restart
Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` returned 'reboot-triggered' immediately, then subsequent call cmd-c971fc44ae194017 confirmed the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-poll boot_id is 1c1541e1-9e5c-4b18-9ef0-9f64443ef8f4, different from the pre-restart d6298ced... value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required data/service (CA trust)
evidence.summary: After reboot, new uptime -s shows later boot time, trust list still shows the CA anchor, cert files intact, and a freshly issued leaf cert again verifies against the system trust store, proving the CA trust configuration survived the restart
